entities.name: COMP
observations: In a pediatric idiopathic-scoliosis case-control study, serum COMP was 11 (5) U/L in 105 cases versus 13 (5) U/L in 103 controls (adjusted p=0.005).

entities.name: Idiopathic scoliosis
observations: The relevant comparison studied children aged 10–16 years with idiopathic scoliosis versus non-scoliotic controls.

entities.name: PMID:25427671
observations: European Spine Journal (2015): serum COMP was lower in children with idiopathic scoliosis than in non-scoliotic controls; 11 (5) versus 13 (5) U/L, adjusted p=0.005.

entities.name: Pediatric serum COMP lower
observations: In children aged 10–16 years, mean (SD) serum COMP was 11 (5) U/L in idiopathic scoliosis (n=105) and 13 (5) U/L in controls (n=103), adjusted p=0.005; assay method was not specified in the abstract.
